# Appendix — every claim this draft may make, with its limitations

Surface `report`, rendered verbatim from `evidence/plan4/claim_ledger.json`.

- [CX-H1-PRIMARY] At a target risk of 20% with 95% confidence and a 20% acceptance floor, neither the QLoRA-adapted system nor the zero-shot baseline could be certified on RAMS: both are Infeasible, so no comparison of certified acceptance between them is possible.
  - _Limitation:_ H1 and H2 collapse to a single test when both baselines are infeasible; this is ONE finding, not two.
  - _Limitation:_ No numerical difference is computed against an infeasible baseline.
  - _Limitation:_ Scoped to the frozen vLLM 4-bit serving stack and to in-domain RAMS.
- [CX-H2-SECONDARY] The secondary confirmatory comparison against the few-shot baseline is likewise Infeasible on both sides.
  - _Limitation:_ Reported jointly with CX-H1-PRIMARY as one finding, never as an independent second confirmation.
  - _Limitation:_ A known harness defect depressed the few-shot arm's confidence score, but it could not affect this outcome: the comparison failed on the QA side, not the baseline side.
- [CX-CAPGAP-01] The infeasibility reflects a capability gap rather than a limitation of the certification method: with an unlimited threshold grid, no finite-sample penalty and oracle threshold selection, the adapted system could accept at most 2.0% of documents at 20% empirical error, against a required 20%.
  - _Limitation:_ A diagnostic, not a certificate: it selects no threshold and certifies nothing.
  - _Limitation:_ The same diagnostic on the development split gives 3.0%, so the conclusion reproduces out of sample.
- [CX-GROUNDING-01] QLoRA adaptation produced a large improvement in grounding fidelity: 95.7% of the adapted system's outputs parse and ground to the source document, against 39.4% zero-shot and 68.1% few-shot, with ungrounded spans falling from 5,355 to 340.
  - _Limitation:_ "Valid" means parseable and grounded, NOT correct: a span can point at real document text and still name the wrong entity or role.
  - _Limitation:_ This improvement did NOT translate into a certified selective guarantee (see CX-H1-PRIMARY); it must never be reported without that null attached.
  - _Limitation:_ Scoped to the frozen vLLM 4-bit serving stack.
- [CX-FEWSHOT-HARM-01] On content-bearing frames the zero-shot baseline outperformed the few-shot one (3,550 against 3,330), and the few-shot arm emitted 63 times more empty frames, indicating that the two frozen demonstrations taught the model to abstain and to continue generating rather than to extract.
  - _Limitation:_ Holds for these two frozen demonstrations, this template and this model; a demonstration set without an empty-gold exemplar might not reproduce it.
  - _Limitation:_ A missing stop sequence contributed to the continuation behaviour but not to the empty-frame rate.
- [CX-SERVING-01] The adapted system's outputs are stack-dependent: the vLLM 4-bit serving stack and the transformers training stack agree on 86.3% of frames under greedy decoding, and 40 of 41 disagreements change the predicted content.
  - _Limitation:_ Measured on train-split frames only; the rate may differ on other splits.
  - _Limitation:_ Divergence is quality-neutral against gold and concentrates in low-confidence frames.
  - _Limitation:_ No threshold was pre-registered for this probe, so 86.3% is reported, not judged as a pass.
  - _Limitation:_ The abstain/extract decision itself flips between stacks at 1.3-1.8% of frames at plausible operating points. Two of the four empty-versus-nonempty flips sit just above the median confidence percentile, so they survive into the accepted set rather than being abstained away, and the flip rate can therefore EXCEED the 1.3% raw rate. The abstention mechanism is stack-dependent at the margin.
  - _Limitation:_ The reassurance in limitation 2 is operating-point-dependent and must not be carried forward alone: at top-90% acceptance divergence is 12.59%, barely below the 13.67% raw rate. The near-zero top-quartile result holds only under aggressive abstention.
- [CX-FEASIBILITY-LESSON-01] The population base-risk ceiling is not a forecast of certifiability: it bounds what an oracle confidence score could achieve, and in this project it allowed 46.5% acceptance where the actual score delivered 2.0%. The empirical risk-coverage curve on development settles selective feasibility at no cost and without sealed data.
  - _Limitation:_ Recorded as a joint process failure: the ceiling was used as a forecast at three separate gates, by both the implementer and the independent reviewer, and the free check was run by neither until after the sealed split was opened.
- [CX-SEALED-01] Certification opened the sealed split exactly once, over 3,152 documents, with a verified hash-chained access record and zero reads of the final or shift splits, which remain sealed.
  - _Limitation:_ The final and shift splits are descoped because no selected policy exists to audit or transport, not for reasons of cost or effort; both commands are free to run.
- [CX-COST-01] The programme of GPU work — inference benchmarking, QLoRA training, prediction generation for three systems over 27,372 frames, and serving-equivalence probes — is recorded job by job and sums to between about $18.7 and $18.9 against an authorised $25 ceiling, each figure derived from the instance's hourly price and the job's measured duration rather than from a billing statement; all certification and analysis ran on CPU at no cost.
  - _Limitation:_ Excludes the value of free-tier and local compute.
  - _Limitation:_ These are operator-recorded estimates from price and duration, NOT billed amounts. No invoice or billing statement is held, so the figure is not reconciled against what Hugging Face actually charged.
  - _Limitation:_ No single committed spend ledger exists. Gate 0 has a per-job artifact; Plan 2's per-job costs live as prose across six documents, so the total is assembled by a reader rather than read off one artifact.
  - _Limitation:_ One paid job has no per-job figure: the first R0 inference benchmark (6a5bcee6bee6ee1cf4ecfe08, 1x L4). Its cost is recovered by differencing two committed running totals, which is an inference and not a recorded figure; the two readings of those totals are what set the width of the band.
  - _Limitation:_ 18 is a floor, not a count. docs/plan2/r0-launch-plan.md records fixes (the nvcc/flashinfer and vLLM prompt-format ones) that could only have been discovered by a job that reached GPU execution and was therefore billed, with no job id or cost recorded anywhere. The recovered $0.15-$0.35 bounds ALL unrecorded pre-R1 spend rather than isolating a single job. The total is unaffected because the running totals capture money regardless of how many attempts produced it — which is a further reason the figure is published as a band.
  - _Limitation:_ Individual figures are themselves rounded as recorded ("about $0.05", "~$11.2"); the total inherits that and is stated to one decimal place, not to the cent.
- [CX-GROUNDING-ORTHOGONAL-01] Grounding fidelity and certifiability are orthogonal for grounded event-argument extraction on RAMS: the QLoRA adapter's ~16x reduction in ungrounded spans over the baselines moved the certifiable frontier by 0.017 for itself and by 0.000 for both baselines, because 87% of its remaining loss sits in output that is well-formed, grounded and content-bearing, and is scored wrong anyway.
  - _Limitation:_ Descriptive only: the decomposition and the grounding-oracle counterfactual select no threshold and certify nothing.
  - _Limitation:_ Conditional coverage under the grounding oracle is not a deployable acceptance rate and is not comparable across systems; the restricted population differs per system.
  - _Limitation:_ The restriction is NOT uniformly generous: it raises the loss of 24 few-shot and 21 QLoRA groups, and a correctness-oracle variant moves the baselines off zero. The baselines' result is carried by the arithmetic ceiling, not by the counterfactual.
  - _Limitation:_ The QLoRA system sits below that ceiling, so for it the ceiling is silent and only the measured curve leaves it short of the floor.
  - _Limitation:_ Scoped to in-domain RAMS under span-exact matching and to the frozen vLLM 4-bit serving stack (86.3% parsed-output parity); portability is not established.
  - _Limitation:_ The certificate bounds average within-group loss, not the absence of error in any document (ADR 0009).
  - _Limitation:_ The decomposition locates loss by CHANNEL; it does not identify the error category that produced it, and this claim no longer asserts one. Until 2026-07-29 the wording said the residual loss was output 'that names the wrong entity' — an attribution whose only source was ADR 0007's unquantified inspection of two development examples, which plan section 12.3 forbids generalising from. Removed on independent review (evidence/plan3/reviewer_record.plan3-close.json, finding O2).
  - _Limitation:_ A measurement points the other way and is recorded here rather than left in the review. On QA's content-bearing certification frames: tp 2,984, fp 4,434, fn 3,797 — false positives EXCEED false negatives by 637 arguments, i.e. systematic over-generation, which is not an entity-naming error. 2,003 of 2,515 error-bearing documents show both fp and fn, consistent with substitution, so 'mostly missing arguments' is ruled out. Wrong-role, boundary and coreference errors share that signature. Plan section 12.1's machine-coded taxonomy is what would separate them and has not been run.
- [CX-ALPHA-FRONTIER-01] On the oracle risk-coverage curve, the 20% acceptance floor first becomes reachable at a target risk of about 0.406 for the QLoRA system, 0.930 for few-shot and 0.981 for zero-shot. Across the whole range below those points no selective policy at any threshold could have cleared the floor, so the infeasibility at the frozen 0.20 target is not an artefact of that particular choice; it holds across everything up to twice it.
  - _Limitation:_ An oracle upper bound with no finite-sample penalty, no grid and no multiplicity correction: usable only to rule operating points out, never to indicate that a weaker one would certify.
  - _Limitation:_ The crossing is a necessary condition, not a sufficient one. A certificate at 0.406 would not issue: at the ~280 groups a 20% acceptance implies, the Hoeffding radius alone is 0.086 to 0.103 depending on allocation, putting the risk upper bound near 0.49 to 0.51.
  - _Limitation:_ Not comparable with the certification rates prior work reports at its own operating points, which are achieved certifications rather than oracle necessary conditions.
  - _Limitation:_ The verdict IS operating-point dependent above the crossing: oracle acceptance for the QLoRA system reaches 0.187 at a target risk of 0.40 and 0.316 at 0.45. The claim is that the frozen target is not a specially unlucky choice, not that no operating point behaves differently.
  - _Limitation:_ The frozen headline target remains 0.20 and no certificate exists at any other point.
  - _Limitation:_ Scoped to in-domain RAMS and the frozen vLLM 4-bit serving stack.
- [CX-WIKIEVENTS-NCERT-01] A WikiEvents certification arm was withdrawn because the corpus cannot support the certificate at any operating point: the preferred method requires 1,386 independent groups and WikiEvents holds 246 source documents across all splits, while the conservative audit is available at that scale but vacuous (Hoeffding radius 0.384 at n = 20).
  - _Limitation:_ A statement about corpus size against the frozen parameters, not about WikiEvents difficulty; no WikiEvents prediction was generated and no base risk was measured on it.
  - _Limitation:_ A descriptive base-risk arm on WikiEvents remains possible and was not attempted.
  - _Limitation:_ RAMS itself cleared the same precondition by only 10 groups, so this is a narrow margin rather than a wide one.
